reply.text:
Yes, most of the time. Ordinary tired from a short night or a long week is usually fine to train through, and a lighter session often beats skipping. A common approach is to keep the session but drop the load or a set or two, and leave a few reps in the tank.

The cases to take seriously are when you've been dragging for several days, your lifts keep sliding, or sleep has been poor for a while. That's a sign to pull back, and a deload week does more for you than grinding. If the tiredness feels out of proportion to your training, that's one for a doctor, not a coach.

Want me to set up something lighter for today?
